entities.name: Infanta Philippa of Coimbra
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Infanta Philippa of Coimbra (1437–1497) was a Portuguese royal princess of the Aviz house, daughter of Infante Peter, Duke of Coimbra, and thus granddaughter of King John I. Her life unfolded amid the mid-fifteenth-century crisis that destroyed her father’s party after Alfarrobeira (1449) and reshaped succession politics under Afonso V.

As an infanta she embodied dynastic capital—marriage alliance potential and commemorative lineage—within a court competing over regency and overseas expansion. Unmarried or conventual pathways were common for princesses when politics blocked advantageous matches.

Philippa’s biography illuminates how Coimbra’s cadet line, once nearly regent-powerful, was marginalised while still leaving women of royal blood in Portugal’s late medieval dynastic matrix.
